CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL PASS â€” audit round 1, commit d536182
(branch sprint-8-duty-to-accommodate-intake), clean tree. Sprint file re-read
fresh in full immediately before this verdict, including the pre-review
adjustments, Chang's wording block, and requirements 11-22.

The core of this sprint is right, and the parts most likely to go wrong did not.
Answers are closed unions in lib/types.ts with no boolean anywhere near them.
The requirement 18 mapping is implemented exactly, including the subtle case:
requestStatus "not-sure" returns insufficient-information and is checked BEFORE
the !== "denied" branch, so an unknown request status can never fall through to
not-applicable. yesNoStatus has no not-applicable branch at all, so
alternatives-explored and analysis-documented cannot structurally return it.
The escalation trigger is narrowed to not-done or insufficient-information per
requirement 20, so an employer with nothing denied is no longer told to request
a functional abilities form. Every artefact listed in requirement 14 is gone â€”
the eslint-disable, the function-level "all three items are currently
insufficient-information" comment, and all three per-item comments. The
Sprint 5 requirement 16 limitation test is deleted outright, not weakened.
All 16 option labels and all four legends and the Q2 helper text match
requirement 16 character for character. Step stays 1 | 2 | 3 and the "of 3"
label is unchanged. buildProsePayload still takes only an AnalysisResult and no
dutyToAccommodate field appears anywhere in the prose path. lib/types.ts changes
are bounded to requirement 21. Vitest 60/60, tsc --noEmit clean, eslint exit 0.

REQUIRED BEFORE SHIP:

1. [MEDIUM] aria-invalid is missing on all four new questions â€” requirement 8.

   Requirement 8 names three attributes for the new questions specifically:
   role="alert", aria-describedby, and aria-invalid. The first two are present â€”
   role="alert" on the shared error at components/IntakeFlow.tsx:783,
   aria-describedby wired through describedById at :625. aria-invalid appears
   nowhere on the new questions.

   This is an omission against an explicit requirement, not an absent house
   convention: the same file already sets aria-invalid on the tenure input
   (:443) and on every narrative textarea (:584). The new questions were held to
   a lower bar than the fields beside them.

   On the fix: aria-invalid on the <fieldset> alone is weak, since assistive
   technology generally announces validity on the focusable control rather than
   on a grouping element. Either set it on each radio input, or give the group
   role="radiogroup" and set it there. Worth doing properly â€” this is a tool
   whose users are employers making a legal decision, and the error being
   announced is the one telling them the form is incomplete.

2. [MEDIUM] Two required Vitest cases were not implemented, and nothing says so.

   Requirement 10 asks for "the conditional question not appearing when no
   denial is indicated". Requirement 22 asks for "Q2 and Q3 rendering for every
   Q0 answer, including no request has been made". Neither exists.

   Both are assertions about rendering, and this repo has no capability to make
   them: no *.test.tsx anywhere, no @testing-library, no jsdom or happy-dom in
   package.json. The nearest existing tests â€” "returns not-applicable when no
   request was ever denied" and the yes/no/not-sure sweep â€” exercise the rules
   consequence of those answers, not the rendering behaviour, so they do not
   substitute for what was asked.

   I confirmed the behaviour itself by reading the JSX, and it is correct: Q1
   alone is wrapped in {requestStatus === "denied" && ...} at :750, and Q2 and
   Q3 render unconditionally at :761 and :771. So the acceptance criteria
   phrased as "QA1 confirms..." are satisfied. The requirements asking for
   Vitest cases are not.

   The resolution is not obviously Dev Team's to pick. Covering these means
   adding @testing-library/react and a DOM environment, and CLAUDE.md's testing
   section specifies unit tests on logic with no in-repo end-to-end tests â€”
   whether that admits component render tests is a standards question for
   Master Controller. What is squarely Dev Team's is that the gap was left
   silent: no note in the commit, no flag, nothing. A requirement that cannot be
   met as written gets raised, not skipped.

3. [LOW] The intake summary shows the user raw union values.

   components/IntakeFlow.tsx:857, :866, :875 and :881 render requestStatus,
   documentationTiming, alternativesExplored and writtenRecord directly, so the
   confirmation screen reads "no-request", "before-decision", "not-sure". The
   human labels already exist forty lines away in REQUEST_STATUS_OPTIONS and its
   three siblings; look the label up rather than printing the slug.

   Not a regression â€” the same summary already prints employmentStatus and
   concerns raw, from Sprint 3. Raising it because this sprint had four
   questions' wording reviewed by Chang for leading and ambiguous phrasing, and
   then echoes the answers back as enum slugs. If the wording matters enough for
   a legal review, it matters on the way back out.

FOR MASTER CONTROLLER â€” not a defect in this diff, and it will block gate 2:

4. Three of Sprint 8's five GroundTruth criteria are untestable as written, and
   it is the same defect this sprint file cites twice as a lesson already
   learned.

   They ask GroundTruth to complete intake and confirm "the checklist reports
   done on those items", "the checklist reports the gap, and that an escalation
   trigger appears", and "the checklist reports missing information and never
   asserts the employer failed a step". All three require a rendered checklist.

   Nothing renders one. Out of Scope says rendering stays with Sprint 6, and
   Dependencies says Sprint 8 blocks Sprint 6, so Sprint 6 has not run. I
   verified this rather than assuming it: no file under app/ or components/
   calls analyzeSituation, analyzeAndPhrase, or buildProceduralChecklist, and
   the only consumer of a checklist item's status anywhere in the codebase is
   escalation-trigger-rules.ts.

   This is precisely the shape CLAUDE.md's gate-2 section describes, and the
   shape this sprint file invokes when explaining why Sprint 5's criteria were
   moved to Sprint 6. Left as written it deadlocks gate 2 the way Sprint 1
   requirement 8 deadlocked gate 1. Either move those three criteria to Sprint
   6, or state that Sprint 8 ships behind Sprint 6 and adjust the dependency.
   Gate 2's honest scope here is non-regression on the Sprint 3 flow plus the
   new questions being present, keyboard-navigable, and validating â€” which the
   remaining two criteria already cover.

STANDING LIMIT: I verified the answer unions, the mapping, the conditional
logic, and that the wording matches what Chang approved. I cannot verify the
questions are the right questions to ask â€” whether "was documentation requested
before the denial" is the correct legal test, or whether these four answers
actually establish duty-to-accommodate compliance. That is law, not code. The
sprint's Dependencies section records Chang's wording review as approved, and
the deferred item (whether Q2 should ask if alternatives were discussed with the
employee rather than merely considered) is correctly left unimplemented per that
same note.

Re-audit required. Finding 2 needs a Master Controller call on component tests
before Dev Team can close it. Do not run /sprint-dev-done on this verdict.

PASS: PASS â€” audit round 2, commit 2642814 (branch sprint-8-duty-to-accommodate-intake),
clean tree.

Sprint file DID change since round 1: blob acf6ed2 -> f778a50. Re-read in full and
audited against the amended text. Worktree blob matches the commit. The changes are
Master Controller's response to round 1: requirement 23 added, requirements 10 and
22 reworded to route visibility testing through it, three untestable GroundTruth
criteria replaced, and a matching standards entry added to CLAUDE.md's testing
section. Both of round 1's structural findings were resolved at the definition
level rather than by asking Dev Team to guess, which is the right sequence.

ROUND-1 FINDINGS â€” all three closed.

Finding 1 (aria-invalid missing). RadioQuestion now renders
`<fieldset role="radiogroup" aria-invalid={invalid} aria-describedby={...}>`
(components/IntakeFlow.tsx:632). The invalid flag is computed per question, not
blanket â€” StepNarrative:711-717 derives one boolean per question, each true only
when an error is showing AND that specific answer is still null. So a question the
employer actually answered is not flagged alongside the one they missed. That is
better than the shared error message implied was coming, and it used the
role="radiogroup" placement rather than leaving aria-invalid on a bare fieldset
where assistive technology would likely ignore it.

Finding 2 (two required Vitest cases not implemented). Resolved via requirement 23.
visibleProceduralQuestions(requestStatus) is exported from lib/intake-validation.ts,
pure, and returns one boolean per question. The component now makes no visibility
decision of its own: grep for `=== "denied"` and `!== "denied"` across
IntakeFlow.tsx returns nothing, and all three consumption points â€” render
(:765), validation (:247), and the submit-time null-out (:303) â€” go through the
same function. That last one matters: visibility and the "was this answer
collected" decision can no longer drift apart, which was a real hazard when the
same condition was written out three times.

The tests land where requirements 10 and 22 now ask for them
(intake-validation.test.ts:92-117). The requirement 10 case sweeps all four
non-denial answers plus null; the requirement 22 case sweeps all five Q0 answers
plus "denied" and asserts both alternativesExplored and writtenRecord visible in
every one, with "no-request" explicitly included as the amended requirement names.
No @testing-library, jsdom, or happy-dom was added â€” package.json and
package-lock.json are untouched this round, as requirement 23 and the new CLAUDE.md
entry both require.

Finding 3 (raw union values in the summary). labelFor() added at IntakeFlow.tsx:828
and applied to all four answers (:879, :888, :900, :906). The confirmation screen now
reads "Yes â€” and it has been turned down" instead of "denied". Falls back to the raw
value if a label is ever missing, which is the right direction to fail.

FULL RE-VERIFICATION. lib/types.ts, lib/procedural-checklist-rules.ts,
lib/escalation-trigger-rules.ts and lib/prose-payload.ts are untouched this round,
so round 1's verification of the requirement 18 mapping, the not-applicable
handling, the requirement 20 trigger narrowing, the requirement 14 artefact removal,
the requirement 21 type bounds, and the prose-payload boundary all carry forward
unchanged. Requirement 16 wording is untouched â€” no option label, legend, or helper
text appears in the round-2 diff. Step stays 1 | 2 | 3 with the "of 3" label intact.
Vitest 63/63, run twice, identical. tsc --noEmit clean. eslint exit 0.

NOTES â€” none blocking.

a) For GroundTruth specifically, since gate 2's criteria now include "labelled":
   role="radiogroup" on a <fieldset> overrides the element's implicit group role.
   Major browsers still compute the accessible name from <legend>, so this should
   be fine, but it is a browser fact rather than a code fact and I cannot settle it
   by reading. Worth explicitly confirming that each question's legend is announced
   as the group's name, not just that the radios are reachable. This is exactly the
   division the new CLAUDE.md testing entry draws, applied to its first case.

b) All four questions carry aria-describedby pointing at the shared error whenever
   any answer is missing, so a correctly-answered question still references the
   error text. Acceptable as built: aria-invalid is per-question, and the message
   names the missing fields ("Missing: request status, alternatives considered."),
   so the combination is unambiguous. Noting it only so nobody reads it later as an
   oversight.

STANDING LIMIT, unchanged: I verified the answer unions, the mapping, the
visibility function, and that the wording matches what Chang approved. I cannot
verify these are the right questions to ask, or that these four answers actually
establish duty-to-accommodate compliance. That is law, not code. Chang's wording
review is recorded as approved in the sprint file; the deferred item â€” whether Q2
should ask if alternatives were discussed with the employee rather than merely
considered â€” remains correctly unimplemented.

Cleared for /sprint-dev-done, then Pipeman. Do not edit the sprint file between now
and dev-done â€” the hash check will refuse, and this sprint has been amended twice.

CONDITIONAL: GroundTruth live test, sprint 8, round 1. Verdict CONDITIONAL.

Everything functional passes. The one criterion QA1 escalated to gate 2 --
whether each duty-to-accommodate radiogroup's accessible name is announced from
its <legend> -- I could NOT confirm with the tooling available in this
environment, and the evidence I could gather leans toward it being absent.
That criterion existed precisely because it cannot be settled by reading code,
so recording a PASS on an unverified accessibility claim would defeat the point
of the gate. Hence CONDITIONAL rather than PASS or FAIL.

ENVIRONMENT
Tested 2026-08-21, Chrome 151, https://bc-employer-issue-guide.vercel.app/intake
Recorded against 791e751. App code byte-identical to origin/main HEAD:
  git diff --stat 791e751 origin/main -- . ':(exclude)docs/**'  -> empty

=====================================================================
THE ACCESSIBLE-NAME MEASUREMENT (the specific ask) -- NOT CONFIRMED
=====================================================================

WHAT SHIPPED (components/IntakeFlow.tsx:632-633), confirmed live in the DOM:
  <fieldset role="radiogroup" aria-invalid=... aria-describedby=...>
    <legend>{legend}</legend>
All four groups: legend IS the first element child (correct ordering for name
computation), and there is NO aria-label and NO aria-labelledby on any of them.

MEASUREMENT ATTEMPT 1 -- authoritative browser API: UNAVAILABLE.
  window.getComputedAccessibleNode -> not a function (flag-gated in Chrome 151)
  'computedName' in Element.prototype -> false
There is no way to read the browser's own accname computation from page script
in this build, so I could not take the direct measurement.

MEASUREMENT ATTEMPT 2 -- extension accessibility tree (read_page).
All four radiogroups render with NO accessible name, and the legend appears as
a separate `generic` child rather than as the group's name:
    radiogroup [ref_83]
      generic "Has this employee asked for a change to their job, ..."
Contrast, same tree, same page: every textbox and checkbox DOES carry its name,
e.g. textbox "What happened, and over what timeframe?".

CONTROL 1 -- native fieldset elsewhere on the same page. Step 1's two fieldsets
have no role override. The tool does not emit a group node for them AT ALL --
the legend shows up as `generic "Employment status"` with the radios as
siblings. So "no name shown" cannot be read as "no name computed": the tool
does not surface native fieldset group names either.

CONTROL 2 -- calibration probe injected into the live page, then removed.
Five fieldsets, read back through the same tool:
  A  <fieldset><legend>ALPHANATIVE</legend>            -> generic "ALPHANATIVE" (no group node)
  B  role="radiogroup" + <legend>BRAVOLEGEND</legend>  -> radiogroup, NO NAME   <-- the shipped pattern
  C  role="radiogroup" + aria-label="CHARLIEARIALABEL" -> radiogroup "CHARLIEARIALABEL"  <-- NAME SHOWN
  D  role="radiogroup" + aria-labelledby -> legend     -> radiogroup, NO NAME
  E  <div role="radiogroup"> + text                    -> radiogroup, NO NAME

WHAT THE CALIBRATION ESTABLISHES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT:
- C proves the instrument CAN surface a radiogroup's accessible name when one
  exists. So the tool is not simply blind to this role, and B's missing name is
  meaningful signal rather than a null result.
- BUT D proves the instrument UNDER-REPORTS: aria-labelledby is a spec-mandated
  naming mechanism and should have produced "DELTALABELLEDBY". It did not.
  An instrument that misses one legitimate naming path may equally miss a
  legend-derived one, so B's silence is NOT proof of an empty computed name.
That asymmetry is why I am not recording this as a confirmed FAIL.

MEASUREMENT ATTEMPT 3 -- the extension's semantic `find` tool. Queried for a
radiogroup whose accessible name is the Q1 legend text. It returned a match and
asserted "This radiogroup has the exact accessible name matching the user's
query, as indicated by the generic element [ref_84] that serves as its label."
I am NOT counting this as confirmation: that explanation describes inferring the
name from the child text node, not reading a computed accessibility property,
and it directly contradicts read_page's output for the same element from the
same extension. One tool inferring a plausible answer is not a measurement.

NET: the criterion asked me to confirm the group's name reads as the legend
text. I cannot confirm it. The strongest statement the evidence supports is
that the shipped pattern behaves differently from an aria-label'd control under
the one instrument that can see radiogroup names at all, which is a real risk
signal, not a proven defect.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING REGARDLESS OF WHO IS RIGHT
<legend> is a fieldset-specific naming mechanism, defined for the `group` role
that <fieldset> maps to natively. role="radiogroup" overrides that mapping, and
legend-to-name support for the overridden role is inconsistent across engines --
which is exactly why this was flagged as unverifiable by code reading. The
consequence if the name is in fact absent is not cosmetic here: entering the
group announces only "radio group", and the option labels alone are ambiguous.
Three of the four groups share the identical option "Not sure / I don't have
that information", so a screen-reader user could answer the wrong question
without any signal. On a duty-to-accommodate intake -- a tool whose subject
matter is disability accommodation -- that is a barrier in the product's own
domain.

TWO REMEDIATIONS, EITHER OF WHICH REMOVES THE AMBIGUITY ENTIRELY (Dev Team /
Master Controller to choose; I am not prescribing):
(a) Drop the redundant role="radiogroup". Native <fieldset> + <legend> with
    same-name radio inputs already maps to a named group and is the
    best-supported pattern; the explicit role buys nothing here.
(b) Keep the role and add aria-labelledby pointing at the legend's id.
Either makes the name correct under every implementation, so nobody has to
resolve which reading of my evidence is right.

RE-TEST NOTE: whichever fix lands, I still will not be able to take an
authoritative accname measurement in this environment. Confirming it properly
needs either a Chrome launched with the accessibility-object-model flag enabled,
a CDP Accessibility.getPartialAXTree query, or five minutes with a real screen
reader (NVDA/VoiceOver). That is worth saying now so the next round is not
scheduled expecting me to settle it with the same tools.

=====================================================================
EVERYTHING ELSE -- PASS
=====================================================================

NEW SPRINT 8 FUNCTIONALITY, tested end to end on the deployed app:
- All four duty questions render on step 3 under the heading "A few more
  specific questions about the accommodation request".
- Conditional gating is CORRECT and I verified both branches. With Q1 answered
  "Yes -- and it has been agreed to", the documentation-timing question is
  absent (3 radiogroups). With Q1 answered "Yes -- and it has been turned down"
  it appears (4 radiogroups) with its four options. That matches the
  requirement-10 rule that it shows only once a denial is indicated -- I
  initially recorded its absence as unexpected, then checked the rule and
  confirmed the app was right and my expectation was wrong.
- Validation ordering: with narrative prompts unsatisfied, only the narrative
  errors fire. Once the narrative is satisfied via the NA affordance, the duty
  validation fires with a specific message, verbatim:
    "Missing: request status, alternatives considered, written record."
- aria-invalid flips false -> true on all four groups when invalid, and back to
  false once answered.
- aria-describedby is set on all four groups when invalid and RESOLVES to the
  live error element (I dereferenced each id and read its text back).
- Each group's radios carry a distinct shared name attribute (requestStatus,
  documentationTiming, alternativesExplored, writtenRecord) -- verified all
  distinct, so no cross-group contamination is structurally possible.
- Completion captured and displayed every answer: Request status "Yes -- and it
  has been turned down" / Documentation timing "Only after the decision was
  made" / Alternatives explored "No, other options were not considered" /
  Written record "No, nothing was written down".

SPRINT 3 REGRESSION -- intact despite the 280-line IntakeFlow change:
- Per-prompt validation: 157 chars in "what happened", prompts 2 and 3 empty ->
  blocked, exactly two alerts naming the two empty prompts.
- "Nothing yet / not applicable" on both remaining prompts satisfied them and
  cleared their alerts.
- Back-navigation retention: values entered on steps 1 and 2, then Back to
  step 1 and forward again to step 3. The final summary shows the original
  step-1 and step-2 values intact -- active / 5 years / No / medical-absence --
  proving they survived the round trip.
- Disclaimer banner present on step 1, step 2, step 3, the blocked/error states
  and the completion screen.
- No analysis, ground, or checklist output anywhere: the completion screen
  matched none of BCHRT / "prohibited ground" / likelihood / anthropic /
  discriminat.
- App console errors: ZERO. Four exceptions appeared, all the known
  "message channel closed" errors traced in Sprint 5 to
  chrome-extension://nbmoafcmbajniiapeidgficgifbfmjfo -- extension layer, not
  the app.

KEYBOARD / ARROW-KEY NAVIGATION -- NOT VERIFIED, and I am not claiming it.
Synthetic key events did not reach the page this session (ArrowDown on a
focused radio left activeElement unchanged and nothing selected), the same
input-transport failure I isolated and documented in Sprint 5. Element.focus()
works, so the radios are focusable, and the structural precondition for native
arrow-key behaviour is verified (one shared name per group, all radios inside
the group). But native roving behaviour itself I could not exercise. Recording
it as untested rather than inferring it from structure.

METHOD DISCLOSURE
Because synthetic clicks and keys were not being delivered, I drove the flow
with real DOM events: element.click() for buttons, radios and checkboxes, and
the native value setter plus a bubbling 'input' event for text inputs and
textareas. These are the events React's synthetic system handles, so real state
transitions and validation paths were exercised on the deployed build, and every
assertion above is against real rendered DOM. It is not identical to physical
input, and the accessibility-tree readings were taken through the extension's
own a11y tooling, unaffected by that.

ISSUES FOUND
1. [MEDIUM, gating this verdict] Duty-to-accommodate radiogroup accessible name
   unconfirmed -- see the measurement section above. Not proven broken; not
   provable correct with available tooling; cheap to make unambiguous.

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL.
Dev Team: apply (a) or (b) above, or supply an authoritative accname
measurement (AOM-enabled Chrome, CDP getPartialAXTree, or a screen-reader pass)
showing the legend is announced as the group name. Then Pipeman reships and I
re-test. Nothing else in this sprint is blocking.
